evidence.field: 考; source account of competing graphic analyses and dated inscription examples, lines 142–149
evidence.text: The database presents two accounts of the graph. In one, early Western Zhou bronze inscriptions use 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’; adding 丂 as a phonetic distinguisher produced 考, usually omitting the 老 component’s lower 匕. A competing account treats 丂 as an earlier graph borrowed for ‘father’, later supplied with 老 as a semantic classifier. The database says early bronze 丂 is used for ‘father’, including 陳逆簠, while it favors the first account as better explaining early Western Zhou 老 used for ‘father’. It cites bronze 考 for father in 兮仲鐘 and for assess/consider in 中山王鼎, as well as Warring States bamboo 考 read as 巧 or 孝. These reported examples establish distinct uses, but do not prove that ‘examine’ developed semantically from ‘father’ or ‘old’.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考 explanation

evidence.field: 考; alternative account of 丂 as a depicted axe handle and early loan, lines 145–146
evidence.text: A different account treats 丂 as the original graph, said to depict an axe handle and borrowed for multiple words including ‘father’; 老 was then added as a classifier to distinguish the father use. The entry says this has some support from early bronze 丂 used for ‘father’, but does not independently establish the depicted object’s name or pronunciation. Consequently, the proposed axe-handle depiction cannot by itself prove the sound basis of the loan.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考 explanation

evidence.field: 考; inscriptional uses and source-reported interpretations, lines 147–149
evidence.text: The entry reports bronze 考 meaning ‘father’ in 兮仲鐘, and bronze use for ‘assess/consider’ in 中山王鼎; it also reports 考 used for 孝 in 孟姬脂𣪕 and personal names. The father sense is often associated with a deceased father but the entry notes exceptions. It cites Warring States bamboo uses read as 巧 and 孝. These are source-reported readings and datings, not direct inspection of the artifacts here. The examples show old graph uses across senses, but do not date the first occurrence of each sense or establish a semantic chain between them.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考 explanation

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, citing 說文解字
evidence.text: The entry recounts the traditional analysis of 考 as an abbreviated 老 plus phonetic 丂 and quotes 說文: ‘考，老也。从老省，丂聲’ (‘old; from abbreviated 老, with 丂 as phonetic’). It explains that the lower 匕 in 老 was commonly omitted in 考. This is an important historical lexicographic account, but the entry also presents a competing account, so the Shuowen analysis should not be treated as settled proof of original formation.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 考 explanation

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 考; variant list, pronunciation, and cited graphic sources, lines 17–32, 45–63
evidence.text: The official entry lists 丂 and 攷 among forms classified as variants of 考, gives Mandarin kǎo, and cites the Shuowen analysis 老省 plus 丂聲. Its discussion of a different variant 𦒱 reports that bronze forms often have 丁 and that a clerical transformation is recorded in 靈臺碑. It does not establish the date when 考 and 攷 became interchangeable or a complete graphic chronology for 考.
evidence.title: A03252 考 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The entry notes that 老 and 考 were used as examples of 轉注 in the Shuowen preface, but says the relationship has remained unsettled. This provides no basis for treating 轉注 as a securely established account of the graph’s formation.

search_audit.outcome: Both official per-character Unihan records were attempted and returned internal errors. The official lookup URL pattern was discovered in the search results; local Unihan readings were checked, but external per-character verification failed.

gaps: Official Unihan pages for U+8003 and U+4E02 were attempted but inaccessible in the web tool. Local Unihan_Readings.txt contains kMandarin kǎo for both; the HSK1 extract does not cover either. Do not interpret absence from that scoped extract as evidence of absent readings.

The local Baxter–Sagart entries support a comparison in one reconstruction system: 丂 *C.qʰˤuʔ and 考 *k-r̥ˤuʔ, with shared MC khawX. A matching phonetic relationship is not established by these forms alone; no paired reconstruction from a second system was verified in this invocation.

Sources report competing accounts of 丂 as a branch, staff, or axe-handle form, and of 考 as 老 plus a phonetic versus a differentiated graph built on a borrowed 丂. The depicted object’s original name and pronunciation are not independently established; an object-name-based sound explanation remains unverified.
No primary oracle-bone or bronze glyph image was visually inspected. Detailed claims about graphic evolution, graphic corruption, or the earliest attestation should remain qualified.

The named bronze and Warring States examples are reported by the opened dictionary, but the exact artifacts and readings were not independently checked against primary editions. The earliest dated attestation of each sense remains unsettled.
Bronze sources reportedly attest 考 meaning father and assess/consider; the semantic bridge between those senses is not established. Do not present a father/old → examine/test chronology as proven.

The search result and official variant dictionary corroborate Shuowen’s account, but Shuowen remains a historical analysis rather than direct confirmation of original formation.攷’s separate Shuowen construction (攴 plus phonetic 丂) and the timing of its overlap with 考 were not independently researched in this pass.
No license or reuse terms for the CUHK database were checked; cite its character-specific page and paraphrase rather than creating a local extract.
